page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-90 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 45 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 177.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of approximately 1.97 GB of memory per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 129122.14 and a PassMark CPU score of 87356.8, both placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. The processor's support for advanced instruction sets is reflected in its top-tier PassMark extended instructions and encryption test results. Single-core performance is strong, scoring 2863.38 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth is highly capable, reaching 215.31 GB/sec for large-block read operations, though large-block write operations perform in the average tier at 78.98 GB/sec.

This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and cryptographic operations, where its multi-core capabilities excel. It also demonstrates strong performance in database operations, static web serving, and medium-sized language model inference. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-highcpu-90 offers high compute density and strong multi-threaded performance per resource unit, making it a viable option for parallel processing tasks that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-90 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance featuring 90 dedicated vCPUs across 45 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores and 177.0 GB of RAM. Designed for compute-heavy workloads, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and cryptographic operations, supported by advanced instruction sets like AVX-512. It also delivers strong memory read bandwidth and high throughput for database operations and static web serving. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.97 GB per core makes it highly cost-efficient for raw parallel processing, though it is less suited for memory-bound applications. This instance is best utilized for high-performance computing, software build pipelines, ray tracing, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
